newsitem.title: UK: Italy's ISAB cuts crude runs as margins sink - trad.
newsitem.headline: Italy's ISAB cuts crude runs as margins sink - trad.

text.p: Italy's ISAB has cut crude throughput at its 220,000 barrels per day (bpd) Melilli refinery in Sicily due to poor returns on refined product sales, traders said on Tuesday.
"The decision was taken last Friday when refinery margins were negative," said an Italian trader.
"They have improved slightly since but are still not enough to cover costs," he added.
Traders familiar with the refinery's operations said the cutback, which amounted to a reduction in crude throughput of 10-20 percent, was under constant review.

Evidence of sliding margins can be seen in the collapsing spread between Russian Urals crude -- a key feedstock for Med refiners -- and heating oil, which has dived from a seasonal peak of over $8 a barrel in November to about $3.50 on Monday.

Traders said persistent strength in benchmark Brent, against which Urals and other regional crudes are priced, was the main problem for refiners which rely heavily on sales of refined products into spot cargo markets.
"It's alright if you've got an inland system but otherwise it's pretty difficult," said a refinery trader.
Other Med refiners were considering similar steps.
"We can't exclude the possibility but we're haven't done the same yet because margins for us are just about breakeven," said a trader for a major Italian refiner.
Dealers said Urals was showing signs of weakening amid ample prompt supply of small cargoes and a lack of demand as dismal margins prompt refiners to delay spot purchases.
"I'm sure you could do (Dated Brent) -80 cents today but we're hanging back because it's going to go to -90 soon," said a refinery trader.
Urals traded last Thursday at Dated Brent -65 and -67 cents a barrel, basis cif Genoa.
Other grades on offer include a couple of cargoes of Syrian Light and end month Iranian Light, traders said.
